clue.text: Huge bird with flap taking off quietly

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: taking something off removes it, so the letter for quietly is dropped from the word for flap

parts.note: a flap is a state of panic
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A huge bird flaps its wings and takes off without a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic is an adjective for something of enormous size or strength, from the giant Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Upset tummy? Enjoy leaving small vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for tummy reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the gut is the belly

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so the letter for small departs from the word for enjoy

parts.note: to boast a feature is to enjoy having it, as a town boasts a castle
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A queasy passenger is relieved to get off a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The less obvious sense of enjoy is meant: to possess something good, which is what boasting a feature means.
explanation.definitionFit: A tugboat is a small powerful vessel that tows or pushes larger ships in harbour.

clue.text: Pay tribute to diet cutting both ends off type of sandwich

indicators.note: cutting both ends off trims the first and last letters away from the word diet

parts.note: to toast someone is to raise a glass in their honour
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone praises a diet that involves trimming the crusts off sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay tribute to' reads as one phrase, but 'to' is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is a British term for a toasted sandwich, usually with a hot cheese filling.

clue.text: Jog in the altogether enthralling grounds, initially

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: in the altogether is an idiom for naked

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of grounds

explanation.surface: A naked jogger running round the grounds holds the onlookers spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' suggests running, but here it means a gentle push.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's elbow is to give it a light push, which is what a nudge is.

clue.text: Bellyache? Go in chippy

parts.note: to bellyache is to complain, and so is to carp
to go in is to enter

explanation.surface: Someone with stomach pain goes into the fish and chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is British slang both for a fish and chip shop and for a carpenter; carp also looks like the fish, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy is informal British slang for a woodworker, one who chips at timber.

clue.text: Cut diamonds found after sea captain docked

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the word for sea captain loses its final letter
found after places the card suit at the end, behind the shortened captain

parts.note: a skipper is the captain of a boat
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Cut diamonds turn up after a ship's captain comes into port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docked' looks like a ship coming into harbour, which suits the captain, but it means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip a class or a passage is to miss it out, just as one cuts a lesson or cuts a scene.

clue.text: Laurel perhaps next to daughter's plant

parts.note: Stan Laurel was half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A laurel bush grows beside a daughter's own plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel' and 'plant' paint a garden, but Laurel is the comedian and plant is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something somewhere is to set or place it upright, just as one might plant a post.

clue.text: This writer's left social worker's grave

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I, and the apostrophe s gives I'm
port is the left side of a ship
an ant is a social insect, and the worker caste does the labour

explanation.surface: A writer reports that a social worker has departed and lies buried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a caseworker; it is an insect from a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave as an adjective means serious and weighty, so a grave matter is an important one.

clue.text: Fork out for five fish

parts.note: pro means in favour of, or for
V is the Roman numeral five
the ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Someone pays up for five fish at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: To fork out is to pay or supply money, and to provide is to supply what is needed.

clue.text: Doctor, regularly tense, seeks bandages

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the next two words is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of tense
the first, third and fifth letters of seeks

explanation.surface: A doctor who is always on edge goes looking for bandages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bandages' looks like a noun, but it is a verb, as in a doctor binding a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress a wound is to clean it and put a covering on it, which is what bandaging it does.

clue.text: More distinguished relative ruddy knocked back

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the word for ruddy is read from its end

parts.note: ruddy means red in colour

explanation.surface: A rather grand relative with a red face has been knocking back drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Grander is the comparative of grand, meaning more imposing, stately or eminent in rank.

clue.text: Accept a little pressure before show

parts.note: taken as written
P is the physics symbol for pressure, a little of the word
to prove something is to show it is true

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take a bit of pressure ahead of a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve a plan is to sanction or agree to it, which is one sense of accepting it.

clue.text: Improving product, essentially, after working with the chaps

indicators.note: after puts the single letter at the end, following the other pieces

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
chaps are men, and the is taken as written

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is kept

parts.note: the seven-letter word has D at its centre

explanation.surface: A product is doing better now that the lads are working on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the mend is an idiom for recovering from illness or getting better generally.

clue.text: Checks rules having lost first of games

indicators.note: having lost the first of a word means its opening letter is removed from the word for rules

parts.note: a monarch reigns, or rules
the first letter of games

explanation.surface: Someone reviews the rules after dropping out of the first of a series of games.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in or check a horse is to restrain it, so reins as a verb means restrains or curbs.

clue.text: Greek character in debt, he taunts

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of debt, all of he and the start of taunts

explanation.surface: A Greek man who owes money is mocked by a creditor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a person, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a written character.

clue.text: Exploit a rude criminal securing release

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the jumbled letters hold the next word inside
criminal means wrong or unlawful, so the letters are put in a crooked order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to be rearranged
to vent is to let out or release

explanation.surface: A boorish criminal is freed from prison and exploits his chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' wants to be a verb meaning take advantage; it is the noun, a daring deed.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold or daring feat, and an adventure is a risky, exciting undertaking.

clue.text: Youngsters sneer and get a rollicking

indicators.note: rollicking means boisterous and wild, so the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Kids sneer at an adult and get a telling-off for it.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a rollicking is also a scolding, which the surface leans on; here the word means boisterous.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers are people aged thirteen to nineteen, and so young people or youngsters.

clue.text: Colour that is rejected on blue quilt

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the first two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is
feeling blue is feeling down

explanation.surface: A colour is turned down in favour of a blue quilt.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a bed quilt, originally stuffed with soft feathers from the eider duck.

clue.text: Again reported what better patient had done

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
a journalist who covered a story reported on it

explanation.surface: A reporter has gone over the story of a patient's improvement once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient who is better has regained health, the sense of having got over an illness.

clue.text: Imps run and disrupt a class

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: to disrupt is to throw into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Little devils run around and disrupt a class.
explanation.definitionFit: Imps and rascals are both mischievous children, an affectionate term for little troublemakers.

clue.text: Risks moving chicanes? Not I!

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not I says the letter I is taken away from the word before

parts.note: taken as written; chicanes are tight S-bends on a racetrack

explanation.surface: A racing driver denies taking risks through the shifting chicanes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chances and risks are both gambles, as in taking chances, meaning acting riskily.

clue.text: Records parrots following end of flight

indicators.note: following puts the word for parrots behind the single letter
end of points to the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the last letter of flight
to parrot is to copy, and so is to ape

explanation.surface: A list of parrots spotted at the end of a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrots' looks like birds after a flight, but it is a verb meaning copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapes as a verb means makes a recording of sound or video, so it records.

clue.text: Talk idly about one very common soldier

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for talk idly goes around the next pieces

parts.note: to prate is to chatter foolishly
I is the Roman numeral one
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone gossips about a very ordinary soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very common' reads as one phrase, but 'very' is a letter and 'common' belongs to the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A private is a soldier of the lowest rank, and common here means ordinary, without rank.

clue.text: Offenders getting intimate in ship

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
inner thoughts are intimate or private ones

explanation.surface: Wrongdoers get intimate aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinners are those who break moral or religious law, so wrongdoers or transgressors.

clue.text: PR bias engulfing a European country

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: spin is the slanted presentation of news by public relations people
taken as written

explanation.surface: Slanted public relations takes over the image of a European nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a nation in south-west Europe on the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: What movie boss gives way?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the guidance a film director provides to cast and crew
second meaning: a route or course to follow

explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as one riddle about a film director giving way, but it splits into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A direction is a course or route, the way someone heads; it is also what a film director provides.

clue.text: Courts shortened trial, supporting District Attorney

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the word for trial loses its last letter
in a down clue supporting means placed underneath, so the shortened word comes below

parts.note: DA is the American abbreviation for District Attorney
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Courts cut a trial short in support of the District Attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' and 'trial' suggest law, but courts is a verb meaning woos.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them, and to date someone is to go out with them romantically.

clue.text: Finest rock group of the 1960s

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the very best part of something
second meaning: the British trio of Clapton, Bruce and Baker

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for the best band of the sixties; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of the milk is the richest part, so it means the finest; it is also a famous late-sixties supergroup.

clue.text: Ace chapter and noble story

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
C is the abbreviation for chapter
a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A tale about an excellent chapter and an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a narrative report or description of events, which is what a story is.

clue.text: Aida perhaps half late for work

indicators.note: half means only part of the next word is kept, the first two letters being dropped

parts.note: Aida is an opera by Verdi
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performance of Aida starts late and the singers have work to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or run, as a machine works or operates.

clue.text: Resists converting nuns

indicators.note: converting means changing the form of something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resists attempts by nuns to convert them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuns are members of religious orders addressed as Sister, so sisters is a name for them.

clue.text: Dazed zebras not oddly making tracks

parts.note: numb means stunned or dazed

indicators.note: not oddly means the odd-placed letters go, leaving the even ones

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of zebras

explanation.surface: Stunned zebras leave tracks on the plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tracks' suggests hoof prints, but it means songs on a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers and tracks are both the individual songs or pieces on an album.
